patch_resolves_note: The fixed build reaches the same bindTo()/closure-destruction path, but `zend_create_closure_ex()` increments the shared internal `function_name` refcount at the bind-result copy. The first closure release still receives the shared pointer, yet the second release is clean because the first release no longer frees the string allocation out from under the original temporary closure.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `bindTo()` creates the second internal closure from `&closure->func`, the copied `function_name` string must gain a counted owner before either closure can destroy it.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the vulnerable original, the second internal closure copy leaves `GC_REFCOUNT(closure->func.common.function_name)` unchanged, so both closure objects alias the same heap `zend_string` while only one counted reference exists. On the fixed original, this same source event executes with the refcount increased before the later destructor releases.

nodes.state: At the first internal-closure destructor release, `zend_closure_free_storage()` passes the same shared `function_name` pointer that was copied into the bind-result closure at `zend_create_closure_ex()`.

At the later destructor release that reaches `zend_string_release()` frame #0, `zend_closure_free_storage()` passes the same `function_name` pointer already released by the unused bind-result closure.

edges.relation: The first temporary closure created from `Closure::fromCallable()` carries the trampoline `function_name` pointer forward as the `func->common.function_name` input for the later `bindTo()` closure copy.
The shared `function_name` pointer copied into the bind-result closure is the exact pointer later released when the unused bind-result closure is destroyed.
After the bind-result closure releases the shared `function_name`, the original temporary closure reaches the same cleanup branch and passes the unchanged pointer to `zend_string_release()` again.
